title: Biggest Billboard
statement:
A city skyline consists of **n** buildings standing side by side, each 1 unit wide; building i has height h[i]. A company wants to paint the largest possible **rectangular** billboard on the buildings. The billboard must be axis-aligned, sit on the ground, and lie completely on the buildings (it cannot stick out above any building it covers).

Print the largest possible area of the billboard.
input:
The first line contains an integer **n**.

The second line contains n integers h[1], ..., h[n].
output: Print one integer: the largest rectangle area in the histogram.

samples.explanation: Use buildings 3 and 4 with height 5: area 5 · 2 = 10.

hints: For every building, the best rectangle with exactly its height extends left and right until the first lower building.
A stack of increasing heights finds, for every building, the nearest lower building on both sides in O(n) total.
The area can reach 2·10^14: use 64-bit integers.
editorial:
Keep a stack of (start index, height) with increasing heights. Process the buildings left to right, plus a final building of height 0. When the current height x is not higher than the top of the stack, pop it: the popped bar of height hh extended from its start index up to i - 1, so its rectangle has area hh · (i - start). The current bar can extend left to the start of the last popped bar, so push (that start, x). Every bar is pushed and popped once.

Complexity: O(n).
